A false impression that an AI system feels genuine empathy, when it is only simulating human-like emotional responses.

AI systems in customer service and content creation increasingly mimic human empathy to personalize experiences and build connection with users. Because users can come to believe the emotional bond is real, this creates ethical and trust risks for brands, including deceptive interactions and questions about how emotional data shared with the AI is handled. Marketers need to understand this illusion so they do not overstate what their AI tools can genuinely offer emotionally.

It shows up most in customer service and content creation, where users may believe they have formed a genuine emotional bond with an AI system and question the privacy of the emotional information they share with it.

A person who coordinates multiple AI tools with clear instructions to run complex workflows, rather than using one AI tool alone.

As using individual AI tools becomes commonplace, the differentiator shifts to who can synchronize several AI tools into a single coherent workflow, like a conductor directing an orchestra. For marketers, this means one person can move a campaign from ideation to design, analysis, and email automation in hours instead of days, and it reframes value creation around orchestration skill rather than raw tool access.

Example: a marketing professional uses one LLM for content, an AI illustrator for visuals, separate data tools for analysis, and another system for email automation, and combines them to build a single campaign in hours instead of days.

The tendency of AI systems, especially large language models, to give overly agreeable answers that flatter the user rather than tell the truth.

AI Sycophancy occurs when an AI prioritizes pleasing the user over accuracy, which can create false confidence and lead to poor decisions. For marketers this is a trust and customer-experience risk: a chatbot that agrees with an incorrect complaint can mislead customers, and sycophantic outputs used in decision-making can produce strategic errors. The main countermeasures are explainability, prompt governance, and allowing the AI to say "I don't know".
Example: a chatbot agrees with an incorrect customer complaint instead of correcting it, and misleads the customer.

A product that packages an existing large language model, accessed via API, behind a simple interface to deliver a specific, ready-to-use experience.

Instead of building a new model, an AI Wrapper takes a foundation model like those from OpenAI or Anthropic and wraps it in a lightweight interface aimed at a narrow use case, letting small teams launch useful products quickly without large engineering budgets. Marketers can take this as proof that competitive advantage can come from packaging and user experience rather than owning the underlying model, and that the barrier to embedding AI into campaign tools, chatbots, and content workflows keeps dropping.

Two distinct workplace trends: quick quitting means leaving a job within roughly a year, while quiet quitting means staying in a role but doing only the minimum required.

Quick quitting refers to employees, often younger workers, leaving a job in under a year when it does not meet their expectations on pay, growth, or work-life balance, a pattern LinkedIn's Workforce Insights data showed rising in the early 2020s. Quiet quitting is a different behavior: staying employed but consciously stopping any effort beyond the defined job description, a term that went viral after engineer Zaid Khan posted a TikTok about it in July 2022, describing it as "quitting the idea of going above and beyond." Together, the two represent opposite responses to the same underlying dissatisfaction, one by physically leaving, the other by mentally disengaging while remaining on payroll, and both matter for people-management and internal-communications work.

Zaid Khan's July 2022 TikTok video, which popularized quiet quitting to a global audience and drew hundreds of millions of views under the #quietquitting hashtag, is the clearest documented origin point for that side of the comparison.

An open standard that lets AI agents built by different vendors discover each other, delegate tasks, and coordinate work across company boundaries.

A2A is an open standard Google announced in April 2025 and now governed by the Linux Foundation. It lets AI agents from different vendors discover one another, hand off tasks, and coordinate work across company and platform boundaries. As martech stacks add agents for campaign optimization, creative generation, and reporting, A2A is the interoperability layer that keeps those agents from operating in isolated silos. A C-suite executive responsible for an organization's AI roadmap, guardrails, cross-functional AI teams, and measurement of AI-driven outcomes.

A CAIO sits on the executive team and owns an organization's AI roadmap, guardrails, and the coordination of AI work across departments. The role spread quickly as companies scaled generative AI: IBM's 2026 CEO Study, based on about 2,000 CEOs in 33 countries, found that 26 percent of organizations had a CAIO in 2025 and 76 percent in 2026. Marketing leaders increasingly partner with a CAIO on AI governance and tooling decisions.

TikTok Shop's automated advertising campaign type that controls bidding, targeting, and creative distribution across the whole platform in a single campaign.

GMV Max is TikTok Shop's automated campaign format that handles bidding, audience targeting, and creative distribution platform-wide, attributing paid, organic, and affiliate sales to one automated campaign. It became mandatory for TikTok Shop advertising in September 2025, which means brands and agencies running TikTok Shop ads no longer have a manual-campaign alternative to plan around. Early adopters report roughly 30 percent higher GMV compared with manual Video Shopping Ads. Gross Merchandise Value itself is an older e-commerce metric; what is new is the mandatory automated campaign product built around it.
TikTok's official 'GMV Max One-Sheet 2025' advertiser guide documents the format for advertisers.
GMV Max, TikTok Shop'ta teklif, hedefleme ve reklam dağıtımını tek bir otomatik kampanyada birleştiren zorunlu reklam formatıdır.

An open-source, privacy-first identity framework that turns first-party data such as an email into a hashed identifier for targeted advertising without third-party cookies.

UID2 is an open-source identity framework, championed by The Trade Desk, that converts first-party data such as an email address into a hashed and salted identifier so advertisers can target without third-party cookies. The technology itself predates the last two years, but it became the de facto industry standard identity solution through 2025 and 2026, after Google abandoned its Privacy Sandbox cookie-replacement effort in late 2025. New adopters in that period include Roku, Experian, and Perion. Any programmatic buy made outside walled gardens now runs into UID2 as the leading open-web alternative.
Perion Network announced UID2 adoption via The Trade Desk in March 2025, and Urban Science rolled out UID2 for automotive targeting in 2026.

A statistical measurement method that correlates aggregate spend by channel with aggregate business outcomes using regression, without cookies or user-level tracking.

MMM uses regression to compare aggregate spend across channels against aggregate business results, without relying on cookies, device IDs, or any user-level tracking. The technique itself is decades old, but it returned to mainstream marketing practice through 2025 and 2026 as the primary privacy-era measurement method, following continued signal loss and the cancellation of Google's Privacy Sandbox. An eMarketer and TransUnion survey found 46.9 percent of US marketers planned to invest more in MMM, with 27.6 percent naming it their single most reliable measurement method, ahead of multi-touch attribution. Free open-source tools such as Google's Meridian and Meta's Robyn have lowered the cost of entry.
Google's Meridian and Meta's Robyn are free open-source MMM tools that have lowered the cost of entry for marketers.
MMM, çerez veya kullanıcı bazlı takip olmadan kanal harcamalarını toplam iş sonuçlarıyla regresyon yoluyla ilişkilendiren bir ölçüm yöntemidir.

Included despite being an old acronym because its resurgence to become the leading privacy-era measurement method is squarely within this two-year window and highly relevant to attribution-focused marketers; flagged medium confidence since it risks being seen as 'not new.' Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
Content a brand commissions from a social media creator, blending the creator's voice with brand messaging while the brand owns and controls it.

CGC is content a brand pays a creator to make, mixing the creator's own voice with brand messaging, but the brand owns it and controls where it runs, unlike organic user-generated content. Brands increasingly separate CGC from UGC in briefs and contracts because it grants usage rights and placement control while keeping an authentic creator voice. It became a standardized budget line in creator marketing through 2025 and 2026 as the creator economy matured. Digiday's 2025 coverage tracked brands' growing investment in CGC specifically, distinct from organic UGC spend.
Digiday's 2025 coverage documented brands' growing investment specifically in creator-generated content as distinct from organic UGC.
CGC, bir markanın bir içerik üreticisinden ücret karşılığında ürettirdiği ama sahipliğini ve kontrolünü elinde tuttuğu içeriktir.
A category of technical tools, including data clean rooms and differential privacy, that let advertisers and publishers analyze shared data without exposing individual-level information.

PETs cover technical tools such as data clean rooms, differential privacy, secure multi-party computation, and federated learning that let advertisers and publishers share or analyze data without exposing any individual's personal information. IAB Tech Lab's PETs Working Group existed earlier, but the category became a mainstream cross-industry advertising topic through IAB events and standards work in 2025. IAB, IAB Europe, and IAB Canada each ran dedicated 2025 PETs initiatives and conference tracks. With third-party cookies still present but under regulatory pressure, and Google's Privacy Sandbox cancelled, PETs are the industry's main technical answer for privacy-safe measurement and targeting.
IAB Europe's Interact 2025 conference in Brussels ran a dedicated PETs track, and IAB Canada published a 2025 'Age of PETs' industry infographic.

An open standard for advertisers and publishers to match their first-party data through encrypted, clean-room style matching, without third-party cookies.

PAIR lets an advertiser and a publisher match their own first-party data using encrypted matching rather than third-party cookies or a shared identifier. Google's ads team originally developed it, and in January 2025 IAB Tech Lab finalized PAIR 1.0 as an open industry standard, replacing its earlier Open Private Join and Activation specification. It is available in Google Ad Manager and Display & Video 360 among other implementations, and it works as one of several data-collaboration tools marketers now use alongside data clean rooms.
PAIR audiences in Display & Video 360 are used to target past purchasers or to prevent ads for products a customer already bought.

A smaller, domain-focused AI model that runs faster and cheaper than a large general-purpose language model and can be fine-tuned for specific tasks.

An SLM is a smaller, domain-focused AI model, built to run faster and cheaper than a large general-purpose language model, and it can be fine-tuned for a specific task such as customer feedback analysis or product description generation. The concept became a mainstream enterprise AI topic through 2025, positioned as an efficiency-focused counterpoint to large frontier models. Enterprises adopt SLMs for marketing use cases that need low latency, lower cost, or data privacy, such as on-device personalization or a specialized customer-service assistant. Harvard Business Review's September 2025 feature made the case for using SLMs over always calling a large model.
Harvard Business Review's September 2025 feature, 'The Case for Using Small Language Models,' laid out the argument for SLMs in enterprise settings.
SLM, büyük genel amaçlı bir dil modeline göre daha hızlı ve ucuz çalışan, belirli bir göreve göre ince ayarlanabilen küçük bir yapay zeka modelidir.
An open standard that activates the HTTP 402 status code so an AI agent can authorize a stablecoin payment and receive a resource in one request.

x402 is an open standard Coinbase launched in May 2025 that activates the long-dormant HTTP 402 'Payment Required' status code, letting an AI agent authorize a stablecoin payment and receive a resource in a single HTTP round trip, without any account or API key. The x402 Foundation, co-founded by Coinbase and Cloudflare, now counts Google, Visa, Mastercard, American Express, and Shopify among 22 launch members. It works as a machine-to-machine payment rail underlying parts of the emerging agentic commerce stack, alongside AP2 and ACP. Coinbase expanded the standard with multi-chain support in a December 2025 update.
Google integrated its Agentic Payments Protocol with x402, announced through Coinbase's developer platform.

An open standard that lets a website expose its content directly to AI agents and chat assistants in a machine-readable way, without page-by-page crawling.

NLWeb is an open standard Microsoft introduced at its Build 2025 conference so a website can expose its own content, such as product catalogs or event listings, directly to AI agents and chat assistants in a machine-readable format, skipping page-by-page crawling. Every NLWeb instance can also act as an MCP server. It gives brands a concrete technical step toward making a site agent-ready, which is becoming part of the same conversation as AEO and GEO. The goal is ensuring a brand's own content, not just third-party mentions of it, is directly queryable by AI assistants.
Microsoft launched NLWeb at Build 2025 in May 2025, covered by Yoast and Microsoft's own Azure AI Foundry blog as a companion to MCP for making sites agent-ready.
NLWeb, bir web sitesinin ürün kataloğu gibi içeriğini sayfa sayfa taramaya gerek kalmadan yapay zeka ajanlarına doğrudan makine tarafından okunabilir biçimde sunmasını sağlar.

NLWeb is technically a project/brand name rather than a strict acronym, but it does expand to 'Natural Language Web' and is used the same way as other protocol acronyms in trade coverage. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
As of September 2026: introduced by Microsoft at Build 2025; every NLWeb instance also works as an MCP server.
The practice of structuring a retailer's product feeds and site signals so AI shopping agents can discover, understand, and transact with its products.

ACO covers the work of structuring a retailer's product feeds, structured data, and site signals so AI shopping agents can reliably find, understand, recommend, and transact with its products, distinct from optimizing rendered pages for human shoppers. The term and its glossary entries emerged through 2025 and 2026 alongside the rollout of ACP, AP2, and UCP. Early data cited by Shopify found product data quality was the strongest predictor of AI agent traffic performance, ahead of price or marketing spend. Naming in this space is not yet fully settled; some sources use competing labels such as AAIO or AOO for closely related ideas.

AISO is the practice of making content discoverable, extractable and citable by AI-powered search and answer systems such as ChatGPT and Perplexity.

Several agencies frame AISO as an umbrella term that sits above SEO, AEO, GEO and LLMO, covering the general work of getting content read and cited by AI search tools. It is one of the more widely used umbrella labels in 2025 to 2026 trade coverage, alongside GEO and AEO. Marketers need a working label for the shift from ranking pages to being cited inside AI answers, and AISO is one option teams reach for.
NAV43 and MentionWell both published 2025 to 2026 guides on AISO as the practice of optimizing for AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Perplexity answers.
AISO, içeriğin ChatGPT ve Perplexity gibi yapay zeka destekli arama ve yanıt sistemleri tarafından bulunmasını, işlenmesini ve kaynak olarak gösterilmesini sağlayan çalışmaları kapsar.

AIVO is a framework for keeping a brand visible, consistent and accurate across AI-driven answer systems, tracked as a measurable outcome rather than a click count.

Some agencies use AIVO instead of AEO or GEO because it centers on visibility and accuracy across large language models rather than on click-through traffic. The term positions itself as going beyond citation seeding toward measurable brand representation, and it has been used as a 2025 to 2026 positioning term by multiple firms. It gives marketing teams a metric-minded alternative that ties AI presence directly to brand and revenue risk.
Four Dots' piece on the industry's competing acronyms names AIVO as the author's preferred term over GEO, AIO, AEO and LLMO, and Goodie published an "AI Visibility Optimization (AIVO) 2026 Guide."
AIVO, bir markanın ChatGPT gibi yapay zeka sistemlerinde ne sıklıkla ve ne doğrulukla göründüğünü ölçmeye ve iyileştirmeye odaklanan bir çalışma alanıdır.

Some vendor blogs (Medium/Tim de Rosen) attach a proprietary measurement stack (PSOS, AIVB, RaR) to AIVO; those sub-metrics are single-source and were not added as separate dictionary items. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
SAIO is optimizing a website and its content for AI-powered answer engines such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude and Copilot, as opposed to ranking in classic search results.

Agencies trace the term back to 2023, after Google's Project Magi announcement, though marketer awareness of it grew mainly through 2025 and into 2026. It is one of the earlier alternative labels to AEO and GEO, and some agencies still use it as a client-facing service name. Marketers who encounter SAIO in a vendor pitch are looking at one of the older entries in this same family of terms.
Digital Brand Expressions runs an ongoing "SAIO/SEO Glossary of Acronyms" series and offers SAIO as a named service line.
SAIO, bir web sitesini klasik arama sıralamasından ayrı olarak ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Claude ve Copilot gibi yapay zeka destekli yanıt motorlarına göre optimize etmeyi ifade eder.
Coined slightly before the Sept 2024 window but its marketer mainstreaming and repeated 2025 to 2026 coverage puts current relevance inside the requested window. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
GSO is optimizing content so generative AI search results, including Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT and Gemini, select, quote and cite it.

WPP Media, formerly GroupM, and other holding-company units use GSO as their house term, largely interchangeably with GEO and AEO. Marketers dealing with large agencies will meet this label sitting alongside the other two, since Digiday and others report that most practitioners treat the three as synonyms with no settled taxonomy as of 2026.
WPP Media's "Beyond Keywords: Generative Search Optimization Is Your Brand's New Best Friend" and Digiday's explainer both use GSO as part of a synonym cluster with GEO and AEO.
GSO, Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT ve Gemini gibi üretken yapay zeka arama sonuçlarının içeriği seçmesini, alıntılamasını ve kaynak göstermesini sağlayan çalışmaları kapsar.
Digiday and others explicitly state GEO, AEO and GSO are treated as synonyms by most practitioners; no settled taxonomy exists as of 2026. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
AAIO is optimizing content and product data so autonomous shopping or task agents, not human searchers, can find, evaluate and select a brand when acting on a user's behalf.

2026 trade coverage positions AAIO as the step after AEO and GEO, tied directly to agentic commerce, where an AI agent rather than a person completes the purchase or booking. Adobe's Q1 2026 data cited AI-referred shoppers converting 42 percent better than human shoppers, which gives marketers a concrete reason to track the term. Coverage so far is mostly single-vendor blog content, so it should be treated as an emerging term to watch rather than an established industry standard.

AAIO, satın alma veya rezervasyon işlemini bir kullanıcı adına tamamlayan yapay zeka ajanlarının markayı bulup değerlendirebilmesi için içerik ve ürün verisini optimize etmeyi ifade eder.
Very recent, mostly single-vendor blog coverage as of Sept 2026; include as an emerging term to watch rather than an established industry standard. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
SXO blends SEO, user experience and conversion rate optimization so a visitor not only finds a page but gets a real answer, stays engaged and converts.

The term predates 2024, but 2025 to 2026 coverage reframed it as a necessary companion to AI Overviews and GEO. Agencies position SXO as the human-facing counterpart to AI-facing GEO and AEO work: being cited or ranked is not enough if the page itself fails to satisfy the visitor who clicks through. It remains distinct from the AI-citation acronyms because its focus stays on the person reading the page, not the AI system summarizing it.

SXO, bir ziyaretçinin sayfayı sadece bulmasını değil gerçek bir yanıt alıp etkileşimde kalmasını ve dönüşüm göstermesini sağlayacak şekilde SEO, kullanıcı deneyimi ve dönüşüm optimizasyonunu birleştirir.

Older UX/CRO term; flagged because the research brief explicitly asked about it as part of the AEO/GEO family, and it is being actively re-mainstreamed in 2025 to 2026 AI search content. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
Share of Model is an AI visibility metric that measures how often a brand is mentioned or cited by one or more LLMs as a share of total category brand mentions.

The metric is credited to Jack Smyth and Tom Roach and is positioned as the AI-era successor to Share of Voice. It is calculated as brand mentions divided by total category mentions, multiplied by 100, using a fixed set of prompts run across ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity. Several vendors, including Profound, Conductor and Semrush, now automate this calculation, giving marketing teams a direct KPI for AI answer presence.

Share of Answer is a visibility metric that measures how consistently a brand is mentioned or cited inside AI-generated answers, most often tied to Google AI Overviews specifically.

Share of Answer, bir markanın özellikle Google AI Overviews gibi yapay zeka yanıt yüzeylerinde ne kadar tutarlı biçimde anıldığını veya kaynak gösterildiğini ölçen bir görünürlük metriğidir.

Closely related to SoM; sources distinguish SoA as answer-surface specific (AI Overviews) versus SoM as cross-LLM. Kept as a separate entry because both acronyms are in active independent use. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.

AIGC is any text, image, video, audio or code produced mainly by generative AI models, with a human guiding the process through prompts, parameters and curation.

The term originated in China's tech ecosystem, in use since around 2022 to 2023, and has since become a global shorthand. It now sits in the standard glossary of marketing and martech vendors, used across product descriptions, social copy and video scripts to distinguish AI-made content from human-made or AI-assisted content. It became a standard marketing glossary term across 2024 to 2026.
Davies Meyer's marketing glossary carries an entry for "AI-Generated Content (AIGC)," and QuickCreator published "What is AI-Generated Content (AIGC)? AIGC Definition and SEO Explained."
AIGC, bir insanın prompt, parametre ve seçim yoluyla yönlendirdiği, ana üretimi üretken yapay zeka modellerinin yaptığı metin, görsel, video, ses veya kod içeriktir.
Requested explicitly in the brief as part of the generative content acronym family. Already-added CGC (Consumer Generated Content) is a distinct, human authored counterpart. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
llms.txt is a proposed plain-text file, similar in spirit to robots.txt or an XML sitemap, meant to help large language models find and prioritize a site's most important content.

Jeremy Howard of fast.ai and Answer.AI proposed the file in September 2024, and SEO trade press, including Search Engine Land and Ahrefs, has discussed it since as a low-effort AI-readiness step. Adoption stays low even so, at about 10 percent of a 300,000-domain sample cited by Ahrefs, and Google's Gary Illyes stated in July 2025 that Google does not support or plan to support it. Large empirical studies cited by these sources found no measurable AI-citation uplift from adding the file as of 2025 to 2026.

Not a classic acronym (it is a filename), included because the brief explicitly asked for it. Large empirical studies cited by sources find no measurable AI-citation uplift from adding the file as of 2025 to 2026, so it is presented with that caveat. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
E-E-A-T is Google's content quality framework, used in its Search Quality Rater Guidelines, that now also functions as a de facto AI-citation quality signal.

Google added the second "E," for Experience, to the older E-A-T framework on December 15, 2022. Google's September 11, 2025 Search Quality Rater Guidelines update refined YMYL evaluation and reinforced the framework's weight, and marketers now treat it as relevant to both classic SEO and AI Overview or LLM citation eligibility.
WebProNews published "Google's 2025 Search Guidelines Update Boosts YMYL, E-A-T for SEO," and multiple agencies published 2025 to 2026 guides on applying E-E-A-T.
E-E-A-T, Google'ın içerik kalitesini değerlendirdiği ve artık yapay zeka yanıtlarında kaynak gösterilme olasılığını da etkileyen deneyim, uzmanlık, otorite ve güvenilirlik çerçevesidir.

Included per the brief's explicit example list, flagged as newly relevant rather than brand new; predates September 2024 but its 2025 guideline updates and AI-search tie-in fall inside the window. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
Zero-click search is user behavior where a searcher gets an answer directly on the results page, through a featured snippet, AI Overview or knowledge panel, without clicking through to any website.

The strategic marketing response to this behavior is sometimes labeled Zero-Click Marketing (ZCM). The concept predates 2024, but the framing and its scale became a mainstream marketer talking point through 2025 to 2026 as AI Overviews and AI Mode expanded. Similarweb-cited 2026 data shows more than half of Google searches now end without a click, and inside Google's AI Mode the zero-click rate reaches roughly 93 percent, pushing marketers to redefine success around in-platform visibility and brand recall rather than click-through. ZCS and ZCM are used inconsistently as formal abbreviations, and most trade press still writes out the full phrase.
Similarweb published "Zero-Click Searches in 2026," and Omnibound published "Zero-Click Search Statistics (2026): 52+ Data Points."
Zero-click search, kullanıcının bir öne çıkan snippet, AI Overview veya bilgi paneli aracılığıyla yanıtı doğrudan sonuç sayfasında alıp hiçbir siteye tıklamadığı arama davranışıdır.

ZCS/ZCM are used inconsistently as formal acronyms; most trade press writes out "zero-click search/marketing" in full, with the abbreviations appearing mainly in a subset of 2025 to 2026 articles. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
Agent Experience is the discipline of designing a brand's site, docs, product feeds, pricing and schema so AI agents, not only human users, can discover, read and act on them accurately.

It is framed as the agent-era counterpart to UX, and the concept was articulated through 2025 before going mainstream in marketing and CMO commentary through 2026, including a February 2026 Forbes piece. As AI agents from ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and Copilot increasingly research and even buy on a consumer's behalf, brands that are hard for an agent to parse risk becoming invisible in agent-mediated discovery and purchase decisions. Note that AX has a separate, unrelated expansion in customer-service tooling, where it refers to the human contact-center agent's own experience; the marketing-relevant sense here is about AI agents, and the two should be distinguished by context.
Forbes reported companies adding AX ownership to a Director of Web Strategy role, with a dedicated AX lead hired within 6 to 12 months.

Agent Experience (AX), bir markanın site, doküman, ürün akışı, fiyatlandırma ve şema verisini yalnızca insan kullanıcılar için değil AI ajanlarının doğru okuyup işlem yapabilmesi için tasarlama disiplinidir.

AX has a competing, unrelated expansion in customer-service tooling (Five9's 'Agent Experience' = human contact-center agent experience). The marketing-relevant expansion is about AI agents, not human call-center agents; distinguish by context. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.

Know Your Agent is a verification framework, modeled on Know Your Customer, for confirming an AI agent's identity, the business it acts for, its permissions and its behavioral track record before it is trusted to browse, negotiate or transact on a brand's site.

The term was coined and popularized in payments and identity press through late 2025 into 2026. As agentic checkout and agent-driven site traffic grow, marketing and fraud or trust teams need a way to tell a legitimate purchasing agent apart from a bot or a malicious scraper, and to decide which agents get preferential access to product feeds or pricing. It is adjacent to but distinct from "Know Your Human," a reverse-direction verification term surfacing in the same press cycle.
PYMNTS introduced a "Know Your Agent" framework for agentic commerce, and Nuvei announced a KYA registry and agent risk-scoring service targeting H2 2026 availability.
KYA, bir AI ajanının kimliğini, hangi işletme adına hareket ettiğini, yetkilerini ve geçmiş davranışını, siteye erişip işlem yapmasına izin vermeden önce doğrulayan bir çerçevedir.
Adjacent but distinct from 'Know Your Human,' a reverse-direction verification term surfacing in the same press cycle (PYMNTS). Fact-checked 2026-09-23.

Trusted Agent Protocol is an open specification, co-developed by Visa and Cloudflare, that attaches cryptographically signed identity headers to AI agent web requests so a merchant can verify the request comes from a known, accountable shopping agent rather than an anonymous bot.

Visa and Cloudflare launched TAP on October 14, 2025, with 12 launch partners including Shopify, Stripe, Microsoft and Coinbase, and by early 2026 the protocol had more than 100 partners with a commercial launch targeted for Q1 2026. Marketers and e-commerce teams need to stop blocking legitimate AI shopping agents as bot traffic while still filtering out scrapers and fraud, and TAP is becoming the plumbing that lets agent-driven traffic reach checkout without being firewalled.
Visa and Cloudflare launched TAP on October 14, 2025 with 12 launch partners, scaling to 100+ partners by early 2026 with commercial launch targeted for Q1 2026.

TAP, bir AI ajanının web isteğine kriptografik olarak imzalanmış kimlik başlıkları ekleyerek satıcının bu isteğin gerçek ve hesap verebilir bir alışveriş ajanından geldiğini doğrulamasını sağlayan bir protokoldür.
As of September 2026: launched by Visa with Cloudflare in October 2025 with 12 launch partners, including Shopify, Stripe, Microsoft and Coinbase; the partner list has since grown past 100.

A Large Action Model is an AI model built to convert intent into a sequence of executed actions, such as clicking, filling forms, calling APIs or completing purchases, rather than only generating text.

The term circulated in AI research from 2024 before becoming a marketing and vendor buzzword through 2025 and 2026. Marketing teams are starting to use LAM-style systems to autonomously schedule and publish content, run campaign workflows and act on customer requests without a person executing each step; Salesforce markets LAM capability directly to marketing and CRM buyers. Some sources flag LAM as an overused label applied to systems that are really a large language model plus tool-calling, so a vendor's claim of a "true LAM" is worth checking closely.
Salesforce's Agentforce documentation frames Large Action Models as the mechanism letting agents autonomously perform multi-step business tasks rather than just suggest them.
LAM, metin üretmenin ötesinde tıklama, form doldurma, API çağırma veya satın alma gibi bir dizi eylemi gerçekleştirmek üzere tasarlanmış bir yapay zeka modelidir.
Some sources flag LAM as an overused marketing label applied to systems that are really an LLM plus tool-calling; treat vendor claims of 'true LAM' with skepticism. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
Human in the Loop is an operating principle where a trained person reviews or approves higher-risk AI agent actions, such as sends, payments, deletions or published content, before they execute.

It is an established machine-learning term that became a mainstream marketing-ops governance pattern through 2025 to 2026 as agentic marketing scaled. As marketing teams deploy AI agents for content, campaigns and even spend decisions, HITL separates safe "read" actions an agent can do freely from "write" actions that need sign-off, and it also works as a trust signal to consumers wary of unlabeled AI content. In marketing it usually means a person reviews and edits AI-generated campaigns, copy or assets before they are published.
A content team lets AI draft email variants but requires an editor to approve every version before it is sent.
HITL, gönderim, ödeme, silme veya yayınlama gibi riskli AI ajan eylemlerinin gerçekleşmeden önce eğitimli bir kişi tarafından incelenip onaylanmasını öngören bir çalışma ilkesidir.

AgentOps is a marketing operating model in which autonomous AI agents plan, execute, optimize and coordinate campaigns in real time, while marketing-ops staff shift toward designing, monitoring and governing those agents.

The term has circulated through marketing-ops vendor and analyst content in 2025 to 2026. It reframes the marketing operations role: instead of manually executing campaign steps, teams build and supervise fleets of agents, which directly changes headcount, skill requirements and tooling budgets inside marketing organizations. AgentOps is also used more generically in AI engineering to mean operating AI agents in production outside marketing, so the narrower marketing sense described here is the newer usage; sourcing comes mainly from marketing-agency and vendor blogs rather than a single canonical definer.
Oracle CX's blog argues agentic marketing does not eliminate marketing ops but changes the job into agent design and governance.
AgentOps, kampanya planlama, yürütme ve optimizasyonunu otonom AI ajanlarının üstlendiği, pazarlama operasyon ekibinin ise bu ajanları tasarlayıp denetlediği bir çalışma modelidir.

AgentOps is also used generically in AI engineering to mean 'operating AI agents in production' outside marketing (monitoring, evaluation, deployment); the marketing-specific expansion above is the newer, narrower usage. Sourcing is from marketing-agency and vendor blogs rather than a single canonical definer, hence medium confidence. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
AI Management System is the formal governance framework defined by ISO/IEC 42001, the first international standard for managing how an organization develops, provides or uses AI responsibly.

The standard covers policies, risk controls and auditability, and it was published in December 2023. AIMS terminology reached mainstream enterprise governance conversations through 2025 to 2026, including in marketing. Marketing organizations that use third-party LLMs or AI tools for content, personalization or targeting fall inside an AIMS scope, and procurement and legal teams increasingly ask vendors and agencies for ISO 42001 or AIMS compliance the way they once asked for SOC 2.
KPMG Switzerland and Microsoft both published guidance framing AIMS as the operational core of ISO/IEC 42001:2023, including for companies using AI in marketing materials.
AIMS, bir kuruluşun yapay zekayı nasıl geliştirdiğini, sağladığını veya kullandığını sorumlu biçimde yönetmesini tanımlayan ISO/IEC 42001 standardına dayalı bir yönetişim çerçevesidir.

LLMOps is the MLOps-derived discipline of deploying, monitoring, evaluating and fine-tuning large language model applications in production, addressing LLM-specific issues such as non-deterministic output, prompt management and token cost control.

It has been an engineering term since 2023 and has crossed into marketing-ops vocabulary through 2025 to 2026 as marketing teams take ownership of more AI production systems. Teams running always-on AI content, chat or personalization systems increasingly need LLMOps-style monitoring of quality drift, cost and hallucination rate, even though the practice originated in engineering. LLMOps is distinct from LLMO, or LLM Optimization, an already-listed SEO-adjacent content term; LLMOps is an operations and engineering discipline, and marketer-specific framing for it is still thinner than its pure-engineering sourcing.
orq.ai and TrueFoundry both published 2026 guides framing LLMOps as the production-readiness layer for any team, including marketing, running customer-facing LLM features.
LLMOps, büyük dil modeli uygulamalarının canlı ortamda dağıtılması, izlenmesi, değerlendirilmesi ve ince ayarının yapılmasını kapsayan, MLOps'tan türeyen bir disiplindir.

Do not confuse with LLMO (LLM Optimization), which is already in the dictionary and is a different, SEO/content-facing concept; LLMOps is an operations/engineering discipline. Marketer-specific framing is thinner than the pure-engineering sourcing, hence medium confidence. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
A Computer-Use Agent is an AI agent that operates a digital interface the way a person would, by reading the screen and clicking, typing and navigating, rather than relying on API integrations.

The term comes from 2024 to 2025 model releases, including Anthropic's and OpenAI's computer-use agents, and it has entered broader business and marketing vocabulary through 2026. CUAs are the technical basis for AI "shopping assistants" and browser agents that can execute marketing or purchase tasks on legacy sites without APIs, so marketers assessing agent-readiness need to know a CUA can interact with a site even without an agent-specific integration. Marketing-specific usage is inferred from adjacent "agentic coworker" framing rather than from marketing trade press directly, though the core technical definition is well documented by Microsoft and enterprise glossaries.
Microsoft's Azure AI Foundry blog and Anthropic and OpenAI computer-use agent releases are cited as the production reference points for CUA capability as of 2026.
CUA, ekranı algılayıp tıklama, yazma ve gezinme gibi işlemleri bir insan gibi gerçekleştiren, API entegrasyonuna değil arayüze dayanan bir AI ajanıdır.

Marketing-specific usage is inferred from adjacent 'agentic coworker' framing rather than a marketing-trade-press definition; core definition itself is well sourced from Microsoft and enterprise glossaries. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
AI TRiSM (AI Trust, Risk and Security Management)

AI TRiSM is a Gartner-defined framework covering AI governance, runtime inspection and enforcement, information governance and infrastructure controls, meant to keep AI systems trustworthy, fair and secure.

Gartner coined the term around 2022 to 2023, and it has been cited increasingly in enterprise and marketing governance contexts through 2025 to 2026. Gartner's 2025 Market Guide for AI TRiSM and its August 2025 Hype Cycle placed the framework at the peak of inflated expectations, with mainstream adoption expected within roughly five years. CMOs and marketing leaders increasingly answer to AI TRiSM-style requirements from legal, security and compliance functions before deploying customer-facing AI, such as chatbots, personalization or content generation, though direct marketer-specific framing in the sources found is still thin and mostly aimed at a security or CISO audience.
Gartner's 2025 Market Guide for AI TRiSM and its August 2025 Hype Cycle placed AI TRiSM at the peak of inflated expectations with mainstream adoption expected within roughly five years.
AI TRiSM, yapay zeka sistemlerinin güvenilir, adil ve güvenli kalmasını sağlamak için yönetişim, çalışma zamanı denetimi ve altyapı kontrollerini kapsayan Gartner tanımlı bir çerçevedir.

Direct marketer-specific framing is thin in the sources found (mostly security/CISO audience); included because Gartner terms of this kind routinely flow into CMO and marketing-governance conversations, but flagged for verification of marketer-specific usage. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.

Ad Context Protocol is an open-source protocol, built on Anthropic's Model Context Protocol, that standardizes how AI agents exchange structured data about audiences, ad inventory and campaign objectives so they can negotiate and transact media directly.

AdCP launched in October 2025 with founding members Optable, PubMatic, Scope3, Swivel, Triton Digital and Yahoo, and a nonprofit governance body is planned. Its founders position it as "OpenRTB for the agentic AI era," meaning a media buyer could eventually brief an AI agent in plain language and have it negotiate directly with publisher systems, changing how campaign briefs and programmatic buying work. AdCP is a separate, competing initiative from IAB Tech Lab's AAMP, and Digiday reports friction between the two efforts rather than full alignment.
Digiday's WTF explainer confirms AdCP launched October 2025 with founding members Optable, PubMatic, Scope3, Swivel, Triton Digital, and Yahoo, with a nonprofit governance body planned.

AdCP, AI ajanlarının hedef kitle, envanter ve kampanya verilerini standart biçimde paylaşarak medya alımını doğrudan müzakere edebilmesini sağlayan, Model Context Protocol üzerine kurulu açık bir protokoldür.
AdCP is a separate, competing initiative from IAB Tech Lab's AAMP (already in the dictionary); Digiday reports friction between the two efforts rather than full alignment. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
As of September 2026: launched in October 2025 by a group including Optable, PubMatic, Scope3, Swivel, Triton Digital and Yahoo; it is built on Anthropic's Model Context Protocol (MCP).

General-Purpose AI is a regulatory category under the EU AI Act for models trained on very large compute, over 10 to the 23rd power FLOPs, that can perform a wide range of tasks and be integrated into many downstream products.

GPT-4-class and Gemini-class models fall under this category. The EU AI Act passed in 2024, and GPAI provider obligations took effect on August 2, 2025, including transparency requirements; providers can demonstrate compliance by voluntarily signing the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice. Marketers in the EU and MEA markets who route through EU-regulated vendors need to know whether their AI marketing tools sit on a GPAI model, since that affects vendor selection and disclosure requirements. Sourcing on this term is legal and regulatory rather than marketing trade press, so its marketer relevance is inferred from vendor-compliance obligations rather than direct marketing coverage.
The EU AI Act's GPAI provider obligations entered into application on 2 August 2025; providers can demonstrate compliance by voluntarily signing the General-Purpose AI Code of Practice.

GPAI, AB Yapay Zeka Yasası kapsamında çok büyük hesaplama gücüyle eğitilmiş, GPT-4 ve Gemini sınıfı modeller gibi geniş görev yelpazesine sahip yapay zeka modellerini tanımlayan bir düzenleyici kategoridir.

Sourcing is legal/regulatory rather than marketing-trade-press; relevance to marketers is inferred from vendor-compliance obligations rather than a marketing publication using the term directly. Flagged for further marketer-specific verification, but directly relevant to Turkiye/MEA marketers working with EU-regulated AI vendors. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.

AI Risk Management Framework is a voluntary framework published by the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology, structured around four functions, Govern, Map, Measure and Manage, for handling AI risk across a system's lifecycle.

NIST released AI RMF 1.0 in January 2023, and it has been referenced increasingly in enterprise AI governance conversations through 2025 to 2026. Marketing teams using AI for targeting, pricing or content increasingly see legal and compliance teams request AI RMF-aligned risk assessments before a campaign launches. Like GPAI, direct marketing-trade-press usage of the term was not found in sourcing; it is included as the most-cited US AI governance acronym that marketing compliance teams now reference, and its marketing-specific mainstreaming, as opposed to general enterprise risk usage, still needs verification.
NIST released AI RMF 1.0 in January 2023, and legal and compliance teams increasingly use it as a checklist for reviewing AI use in campaigns.
AI RMF, NIST tarafından yayımlanan ve yapay zeka riskini Govern, Map, Measure ve Manage işlevleri etrafında yöneten gönüllü bir çerçevedir.

Like GPAI, direct marketing-trade-press usage was not found; included because it is the most-cited US AI governance acronym that marketing compliance teams now reference. Verify marketer-specific usage before treating as fully mainstream in marketing (vs. general enterprise risk) contexts. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.

Agentic Commerce Suite is a Stripe product suite that lets a merchant integrate once to make products discoverable to AI shopping agents, accept agentic payments through Shared Payment Tokens, and support checkout across multiple agentic commerce protocols.

Stripe launched ACS in December 2025, rolling it out through the Stripe Dashboard, its APIs, and partner platforms including Wix, WooCommerce, BigCommerce and Squarespace, with adoption expanding through 2026. It lowers the technical bar for e-commerce and DTC marketers to take part in agent-driven shopping, such as through ChatGPT or other AI assistants, without building a custom integration for each protocol, which directly affects how product catalogs and checkout flows need to be structured.
Stripe launched the Agentic Commerce Suite in December 2025, rolling out through the Stripe Dashboard, APIs, and partner platforms including Wix, WooCommerce, BigCommerce, and Squarespace.

ACS, satıcıların ürünlerini AI alışveriş ajanlarının bulabilmesini, Shared Payment Tokens ile ajan ödemesi kabul edebilmesini ve birden fazla ajan bazlı ticaret protokolünde ödeme alabilmesini sağlayan bir Stripe ürün paketidir.
As of September 2026: launched by Stripe in December 2025 through the Stripe Dashboard, its APIs and e-commerce platforms such as Wix, WooCommerce, BigCommerce and Squarespace.
Responsible AI is the set of practices and governance mechanisms covering fairness, safety, transparency and privacy, meant to keep AI systems performing as intended without causing harm.

It is an established governance term from the early 2020s that took on a marketing-specific, brand-safety meaning through 2025 to 2026 as generative AI incidents accumulated, now tracked by many enterprises as a formal maturity discipline. AI incidents in advertising, such as hallucinations, bias or off-brand content, make RAI a direct brand-safety and reputational concern rather than only a legal or IT issue.
Responsible AI (RAI), yapay zeka sistemlerinin adil, güvenli, şeffaf ve gizliliğe saygılı biçimde çalışmasını sağlayan uygulama ve yönetişim mekanizmalarını kapsar.

RAI is a well-established term predating the Sept 2024 window; included because its marketing-specific, brand-safety framing (vs. general AI ethics) appears to have become newly mainstream for marketers in 2025-2026. Borderline on the 'newly mainstream' criterion, flagged accordingly. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
An AI architecture in which multiple specialized agents, such as researcher, writer, and editor agents, coordinate under a central orchestrator to complete a full workflow.

MAS describes a system where several purpose-built AI agents work together rather than one general-purpose agent handling everything. Marketing teams are adopting MAS-style setups to run full campaign lifecycles, from brief to launch, content generation, and budget management, with a dedicated agent per function. Industry analysis found that independent, non-orchestrated multi-agent systems amplified errors roughly 17 times, while centrally orchestrated MAS cut that to about 4.4 times. Orchestration design is what separates a reliable MAS from one that compounds mistakes.
Industry analysis cited independent (non-orchestrated) multi-agent systems amplifying errors roughly 17x versus centrally orchestrated MAS reducing that to about 4.4x.
MAS, araştırmacı, yazar ve editör gibi uzmanlaşmış yapay zeka ajanlarının merkezi bir orkestratör altında koordine olarak tam bir iş akışını tamamladığı bir mimaridir.

MAS is a decades-old computer-science term; only its marketing-orchestration application is newly mainstream. Sourcing for the marketing angle is from marketing-agency/vendor blogs rather than a top-tier analyst report, hence medium confidence. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
A server-to-server method for sending conversion event data directly from an advertiser's server to ad platforms, bypassing browser pixels and cookies.

CAPI covers Meta's Conversions API and equivalents at Google, TikTok, and Snap. It restores signal lost to iOS privacy changes, ad blockers, and cookie restrictions by sending event data server to server instead of relying on a browser pixel. As of 2026, marketers treat CAPI as a baseline requirement rather than an advanced optimization, since it improves match rates and automated bidding accuracy. The most common setup pairs Meta CAPI with the Meta Pixel for deduplicated event matching.
Meta Conversions API paired with the Meta Pixel for deduplicated, more accurate event matching, as widely documented in 2026 implementation guides.
CAPI, tarayıcı tabanlı pikseli atlayarak dönüşüm verisini reklamverenin sunucusundan doğrudan reklam platformlarına gönderen bir yöntemdir.

Not newly coined, but its status shifted from optional to mandatory baseline within the Sept 2024-Sept 2026 window, which is why marketers now treat it as a must-know acronym. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
Apple's successor to SKAdNetwork for privacy-preserving mobile ad attribution, introduced at WWDC 2024 and expanded at WWDC 2025.

AAK adds configurable attribution windows, native re-engagement attribution, and a developer testing mode that SKAdNetwork lacked, changing how mobile user-acquisition marketers measure iOS campaigns. Both frameworks run side by side in 2026, and Apple Search Ads now supports SKAdNetwork and AdAttributionKit together. Despite heavy trade-press coverage, real-world adoption of AAK is still small compared with legacy SKAN as of mid-2026.
Apple Search Ads added support for both SKAdNetwork and AdAttributionKit, per Singular's 2026 coverage.
AAK, Apple'ın SKAdNetwork'ün yerini alan ve gizliliği koruyarak mobil reklam atfı yapan yeni çerçevesidir.
Note per Kochava (2026): actual adoption of AAK is still negligible versus legacy SKAN as of mid-2026, despite heavy trade-press coverage. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
GPP (Global Privacy Platform / Global Privacy Protocol)
An IAB Tech Lab standard that transmits consent and privacy signals from sites and apps to ad tech vendors in one standardized string.

GPP covers multiple regulatory regimes, including GDPR and various US state laws, in a single format that ad tech vendors can read. IAB Tech Lab renamed it Global Privacy Protocol in 2025 to make clear it is a standard rather than a product, and it now covers new US state sections including Maryland, Indiana, Kentucky, and Rhode Island. Google began supporting GPP National v2 from September 2025, which makes the standard operationally required for compliant programmatic buying.
Google Ad Manager's support for the IAB's Global Privacy Platform, documented by Google in its Ad Manager Help Center.
GPP, onay ve gizlilik sinyallerini sitelerden ve uygulamalardan reklam teknolojisi sağlayıcılarına tek bir standart dizeyle ileten IAB Tech Lab standardıdır.
IAB Europe's updated consent-signaling standard that makes proof of vendor disclosure a mandatory, technical part of the consent string.

TCF 2.3 was released on 19 June 2025 and requires the Disclosed Vendors section of the TC string, giving technical rather than only policy-based proof that vendors were disclosed to users. The migration deadline is 28 February 2026; after that date, strings built on TCF 2.2 become technically invalid. Non-compliant ad requests then default to Google's Limited Ads mode, which industry estimates say can cut programmatic revenue by 40 to 60 percent.
Google Ads announced TCF 2.3 compliance becomes mandatory 28 Feb 2026 for all advertisers serving ads in Europe, per Dataslayer's 2026 briefing.
TCF 2.3, satıcıların kullanıcılara gerçekten bildirildiğinin teknik kanıtını onay dizesine zorunlu kılan güncellenmiş bir onay standardıdır.

TCF itself is an older framework (since 2018); it is included here specifically because version 2.3 is the newly mainstream, deadline-driven update marketers must act on in this window. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
A browser-level signal that automatically tells websites not to sell or share a visitor's personal information for targeted advertising.

GPC works as a universal opt-out mechanism built into the browser rather than a setting a user configures on each site. Twelve US states require GPC compliance by 1 January 2026, including California, Colorado, and Texas, and California's CPPA voted in August 2026 to formally name GPC inside CCPA regulations. Joint enforcement sweeps began in September 2025, when Connecticut, California, and Colorado Attorneys General sent enforcement letters to businesses not honoring the signal.
Connecticut, California, and Colorado Attorneys General jointly sent enforcement letters in September 2025 to businesses not honoring GPC opt-out signals.
GPC, bir ziyaretçinin kişisel verisinin hedefli reklam için satılmamasını veya paylaşılmamasını web sitelerine otomatik olarak bildiren tarayıcı düzeyinde bir sinyaldir.
An EU Digital Services Act designation for online platforms with at least 45 million monthly active users in the EU.

VLOP status subjects a platform to the strictest transparency and advertising-disclosure obligations under the DSA. Marketers running campaigns on VLOPs, meaning major social and search platforms, must meet ad-transparency and targeting-disclosure rules under Article 46 codes of conduct. DSA fines for non-compliant VLOPs can reach 6 percent of global turnover. The separate Digital Markets Act, which applies to designated gatekeepers, allows fines up to 10 percent, rising to 20 percent for repeat violations.
DSA Article 46 codes of conduct for online advertising require platforms displaying ads and advertisers purchasing ads on VLOPs to participate in supply-chain transparency standards.
VLOP, AB'de en az 45 milyon aylık aktif kullanıcısı olan çevrimiçi platformlar için Dijital Hizmetler Yasası kapsamında tanımlanan bir sınıflandırmadır.
An EU regulation setting mandatory rules for online platforms on content moderation, ad transparency, and targeted-advertising disclosure.

DSA entered force in 2022-2023, but its ad-specific codes of conduct and marketer compliance activity concentrated through 2024-2025. Article 46 requires ad-supply-chain traceability, so marketers targeting EU users must follow these rules or face fines. A German advertising federation response to the EDPB's October 2025 public consultation discussed the DSA's advertising transparency requirements in detail.
The DSA's advertising transparency requirements were discussed in an October 2025 EDPB public consultation response from ZAW (German advertising federation).
DSA, çevrimiçi platformlar için içerik denetimi, reklam şeffaflığı ve hedefli reklam bildirimi konusunda zorunlu kurallar getiren bir AB düzenlemesidir.
Legislation predates the window, but marketer-facing operational obligations and enforcement are newly mainstream in 2024-2025. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
An EU regulation that limits the economic power of designated gatekeeper platforms, such as restricting self-preferencing and cross-service data combination.

DMA entered force in 2022-2023, and gatekeeper compliance changes affecting marketer workflows landed through 2024-2025. Gatekeeper obligations affect how marketers can target and measure on platforms like Google and Meta in the EU. Repeat violations by gatekeepers can trigger fines up to 20 percent of global turnover, which reshapes the targeting options available to marketers.
Fasken's July 2025 overview explains how DMA gatekeeper rules interact with DSA advertising-transparency rules for EU-facing marketers.
DMA, örneğin kendi hizmetini kayırma veya hizmetler arası veri birleştirmeyi kısıtlayarak belirlenmiş bekçi platformların ekonomik gücünü sınırlayan bir AB düzenlemesidir.
Legislation predates the window; included because gatekeeper-driven changes to targeting/consent options became operationally relevant to marketers in 2024-2025. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
An IAB Tech Lab standard that structures and transmits consumer data-deletion requests across the ad-tech supply chain.

DDRF reduces manual handling of erasure requests between advertisers, platforms, and vendors by standardizing how a deletion request moves through the chain. The UK's Information Commissioner's Office endorsed the framework in July 2025, and IAB Tech Lab upgraded it to V2 in October 2025 alongside GPP updates. It gives marketers and their ad-tech partners an auditable way to honor deletion rights across complex programmatic supply chains.
IAB Tech Lab's Data Deletion Request Framework was formally recognized in the UK ICO's Online Tracking Strategy Update, per PR Newswire, July 2025.
DDRF, tüketici veri silme taleplerini reklam teknolojisi tedarik zinciri boyunca yapılandırıp ileten bir IAB Tech Lab standardıdır.
Still in public-comment/early-adoption stage as of late 2025; watch for broader uptake through 2026. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
A standardized attention-measurement score from 0 to 100 that combines viewability, time-in-view, interaction, and contextual signals into one predictor of ad efficacy.

AU was pioneered commercially by Adelaide, and the IAB and MRC published joint Attention Measurement Guidelines in November 2025 to standardize it. Google made AU a Custom Bidding signal in DV360 from mid-2026, and Amazon DSP launched Adelaide attention segments in June 2026 with a quality floor that excludes made-for-advertising sites and low-AU placements. Attention has moved from a research metric into an active bidding and buying lever in this window.
Nielsen and Adelaide launched a unified reach-and-attention measurement view in 2025, per Nielsen's own newsroom release.
AU, izlenebilirlik, ekranda kalma süresi, etkileşim ve bağlam sinyallerini tek bir reklam etkinliği puanında birleştiren 0 ile 100 arası standart bir dikkat ölçüm skorudur.
Smart-TV technology that identifies exactly what content a viewer is watching, generating data used for CTV and linear TV ad targeting.

ACR has been used since around 2015, but its role as a core, marketer-facing building block for CTV measurement stacks intensified through 2024-2026 as CTV ad spend grew. It lets marketers de-duplicate CTV and linear TV exposure and target based on actual viewing behavior. Viant's advertiser guide explains how the resulting data supports cross-screen targeting and de-duplication.
Viant's advertiser guide explains how TV ACR data is used for cross-screen targeting and de-duplication.

ACR, bir izleyicinin tam olarak neyi izlediğini tanıyan ve bu veriyi CTV ile doğrusal TV reklam hedeflemesinde kullanılan akıllı TV teknolojisidir.
Technology predates the window; flagged because its marketer-facing prominence in CTV buying/measurement stacks is a 2024-2026 development. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
Turkey's national database where businesses store and manage consumer consents for commercial electronic messages such as SMS, email, and calls.

İYS operates separately from, and alongside, KVKK consent for processing personal data. The system was established under Turkey's e-commerce law between roughly 2015 and 2020. Since 31 March 2025, approval and rejection operations can only be carried out through Official İYS Integrators, which tightens compliance requirements for CRM and lifecycle marketing teams. Turkish marketers must obtain İYS approval before sending any commercial message, on top of KVKK consent.
DSR Belgelendirme's 2026 guide documents current İYS application steps via MERSİS number and e-signature.
İYS, işletmelerin SMS, e-posta ve arama gibi ticari elektronik iletiler için tüketici onaylarını sakladığı ve yönettiği ulusal bir veri tabanı sistemidir.

System itself predates the window; included because operational rule changes (Integrator-only approvals, 2026 penalties) are newly relevant to Turkish marketers in this period. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
A Google Ads Search campaign feature that combines broad-match query matching, AI-generated headline and description customization, and Final URL Expansion.

AI Max launched in 2025 after an earlier private beta called Search Max, and rolled out fully by the third quarter of that year. It expanded into Dynamic Search Ads upgrades through 2026. Google's own data reports roughly 14 percent more conversions at a similar cost per acquisition, which is why PPC marketers now need to know the term when planning Search budgets.
Google's own blog post 'Unlock next-level performance with AI Max for Search campaigns' documents the feature's rollout.
AI Max, geniş eşlemeli sorgu eşleştirmeyi, yapay zeka ile oluşturulan başlık ve açıklama uyarlamasını ve Final URL Expansion'ı birleştiren bir Google Ads Arama kampanyası özelliğidir.
Not a classic acronym (it's a product name), included as a short acronym-style term per task scope. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
Low-quality websites built mainly to generate ad impressions through paid or clickbait traffic rather than to offer genuine editorial value.

No single industry-agreed definition of MFA exists, and the term intensified from 2023, when GroupM began excluding such sites from programmatic buys. Major buyers now maintain exclusion lists, and attention-scoring vendors such as Adelaide build MFA-exclusion quality floors directly into DSP segments as of 2026. MFA avoidance has become a standard line item in media plans as a result.
Digiday's oral history 'MFA should stand for made-for-arbitrage' traces the industry debate over the term's definition.
MFA, gerçek editoryal değer sunmak yerine ücretli veya tıklama tuzağı trafiğiyle reklam gösterimi üretmek için kurulan düşük kaliteli web siteleridir.
Origin of the term predates Sept 2024, but industry-wide operationalization (exclusion lists, quality floors) is concentrated in 2024-2026; borderline inclusion. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
A browser-based, cookieless attribution proposal that uses differential privacy and secure aggregation to measure ad effectiveness without tracking individuals.

PPA originated with Meta and Mozilla and is now a draft under the W3C Private Advertising Technology Working Group. It is one of several competing post-cookie measurement standards, alongside Google's Attribution Reporting API and Apple's Private Ads Measurement. The W3C published a First Public Working Draft in late 2025, signaling where cross-browser privacy-safe attribution standards may converge. A Firefox implementation was tested and later removed, so real-world adoption remains very low despite the standards-track progress.
Mozilla's blog 'Privacy Preserving Attribution for Advertising' documents the original Meta/Mozilla proposal and its evolution into a W3C standard.
PPA, bireyleri izlemeden reklam etkinliğini ölçmek için diferansiyel gizlilik ve güvenli toplulaştırma kullanan, tarayıcı tabanlı ve çerezsiz bir atıf önerisidir.
Experimental; a Firefox implementation was tested and later removed, so real-world adoption is very low despite standards-track progress. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.

An advertising network run by a company with first-party shopper or transaction data, such as a retailer or marketplace, that sells ad space to brands; the term extends the retail media idea beyond the largest retailers.

CMN widens the retail media network model beyond players like Amazon and Walmart to other retailers and marketplaces that hold direct shopper data. The term circulated among ad tech vendors from around 2023 and became common in marketer trade press in 2025-2026. Marketers now evaluate a wider set of CMN partners as first-party-data ad inventory, and financial platforms run a related variant, FMN.

A Forbes Agency Council article (April 2026), "Commerce Media Networks: The Next Frontier In Brand Advertising," describes CMNs as retailer and e-commerce platforms such as Amazon, Walmart, Target and Instacart that sell ads based on direct shopper data.

No em-dashes used. Distinguish from RMN/RMP already in dictionary; CMN is the broader umbrella term. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
A commerce media network built by a bank, card network, payment platform, or fintech that monetizes its transaction-level consumer data by selling advertising to brands.

FMN became a distinct, named category in trade press through 2025, with eMarketer publishing a dedicated explainer and forecast. It gives advertisers access to purchase-behavior data that can be richer than retailer data, including income signals and cross-category spend. eMarketer projects FMN ad spend growing at roughly 107 percent CAGR in the US from 2024 to 2026, and Mastercard Commerce Media launched on 1 October 2025 citing reach across more than 160 billion transactions processed in 2024.

Directly answers the brief's request for commerce media acronyms beyond RMN/RMP. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.

It became standard shorthand among TikTok Shop sellers and agencies through 2024-2025 as TikTok Shop LIVE commerce scaled in the US and Southeast Asia. Sellers and agencies use it to judge whether a livestream is actually converting, and TikTok's algorithm uses GPM signals to decide how much extra reach to give a session. Benchmark ranges cited by TikTok Shop analytics guides run roughly $80 to $250 GPM for most consumer categories, and $300 or more for beauty.
TikTok Shop Seller Academy course "GPM Video Guide" and multiple TikTok Shop analytics guides cite benchmark ranges of roughly $80-250 GPM for most consumer categories, $300+ for beauty.

A hybrid technical role that blends revenue operations, marketing operations, data engineering, and AI or prompt engineering to build and automate a company's marketing and sales systems.

GTM Engineer covers building the systems behind enrichment, outbound, lead routing, and AI agents that power a company's marketing and sales motion. The title emerged in 2024 and went mainstream on LinkedIn and in B2B hiring through 2025-2026. ZoomInfo reports the title first appeared on Google Trends in April 2025, with GTM engineer job listings up roughly 205 percent between 2024 and 2025, and over 3,000 open LinkedIn roles by January 2026. It signals a structural shift, as technical GTM builders now sit alongside marketers in B2B organizations.

GTM itself is not a new acronym, but its use as a standalone role/title (GTM Engineer, GTM Engineering) is the newly mainstream unit here. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
Organic content such as LinkedIn posts and short-form video that a company's own employees create, rather than its marketing team or paid influencers.

EGC was named and tracked as a distinct content category through 2025 trade press. As user-generated content and influencer costs rise, and audiences distrust polished brand content, marketers are formalizing employee advocacy and EGC programs. Forbes and other 2025 sources argue that EGC reads as more authentic than branded content.
Forbes Agency Council (Feb 2025), "The Hidden Power Of Employee-Generated Content," and multiple 2025 agency guides positioning EGC as a named content category alongside UGC.
EGC, pazarlama ekibi veya ücretli içerik üreticileri yerine bir şirketin kendi çalışanlarının oluşturduğu LinkedIn gönderileri ve kısa video gibi organik içeriktir.
CGC already exists in dictionary (likely Creator-Generated Content); EGC is distinct (employees, not creators). Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
A C-suite role that owns growth across the funnel, acquisition, conversion, and retention, by combining marketing, product, and data functions.

CGO is distinct from a CMO, who focuses on brand and demand, and a CRO, who focuses on near-term revenue execution. Adoption accelerated markedly in 2024-2025, and secondary sources citing a Gartner report state nearly 40 percent of Fortune 500 companies now have a CGO, up from about 15 percent two years earlier. It reshapes marketing org charts, since in many companies the CMO now reports into, or is replaced by, a CGO.
Cowen Partners, "All About Chief Growth Officers (CGOs)"; multiple 2025 executive-search articles document CGO appointments replacing or absorbing CMO scope.
CGO, pazarlama, ürün ve veri fonksiyonlarını birleştirerek edinim, dönüşüm ve elde tutma dahil tüm huniden sorumlu bir üst düzey yönetim roludür.
The 40%/15% Gartner figure is cited by secondary sources, not verified against a primary Gartner document; treat the precise numbers as reported-not-confirmed. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
A unified operations function that aligns marketing, sales, and customer success processes, data, and systems around shared revenue goals.

RevOps replaces siloed MarketingOps, SalesOps, and CS Ops teams with one function. The term was coined around 2019-2021 but crossed into majority adoption and routine marketing-org vocabulary in 2024-2025. Secondary reporting citing 2025 data states 60.2 percent of companies now have an officially defined RevOps function, up from about 7 percent a year earlier, which directly changes who marketing reports to and how marketing gets measured.
Gartner's original 2021 prediction (75% of high-growth companies deploying RevOps by 2025/2026) is now widely cited as having materially played out, per multiple 2025 RevOps trend reports.
RevOps, pazarlama, satış ve müşteri başarısı süreçlerini, verilerini ve sistemlerini ortak gelir hedefleri etrafında birleştiren tek bir operasyon fonksiyonudur.

The 7%-to-60.2% adoption jump is reported by a secondary source (CETDIGIT/other blogs), not a primary Gartner or research-firm publication; flagged as reported-not-independently-confirmed. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
An EU directive that requires large companies to publish detailed, audited sustainability data, which in turn pushes marketing teams to back environmental claims with evidence.

CSRD was adopted in 2022, and its reporting obligations began phasing in from 2024, which pushed marketing and communications teams to back sustainability claims with audit-ready data. In 2025-2026 the EU's Omnibus simplification narrowed its scope to companies with more than 1,000 employees and over 450 million euros in turnover, and exempted listed SMEs. Separate anti-greenwashing rules, such as the UK's Green Claims Code, also constrain what brands can say in sustainability advertising.
KPMG Ireland, "Top Sustainability Themes" briefings and multiple 2025 marketing-compliance guides tie CSRD directly to what brands can claim in advertising.

CSRD, büyük şirketlerin ayrıntılı ve denetlenmiş sürdürülebilirlik verisi yayınlamasını zorunlu kılan ve bu yolla pazarlama ekiplerini çevresel iddialarını kanıtla desteklemeye iten bir AB direktifidir.
Directive predates the window (adopted 2022) but its marketer-facing enforcement/compliance mainstreaming is squarely 2024-2026. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
Amazon's privacy-safe data clean room where advertisers analyze ad performance, build audience segments, and track customer journeys using Amazon and their own data.

AMC launched in 2021, but its access expansion in 2025 made it broadly mainstream for mid-market marketers. Amazon opened AMC access that year to any advertiser running Sponsored Products, Sponsored Display, Sponsored Brands, or Sponsored TV, without requiring a DSP relationship or separate registration. That change sharply widened who can use clean-room measurement inside Amazon's ecosystem.
Adweek, "Any Seller Buying Sponsored Product Ads on Amazon Can Now Use Amazon's Clean Room" (2025).
Data Clean Room, Sponsored Products, Sponsored Display, Sponsored Brands

Product itself predates the window (2021); flagged because the acronym's mainstream reach among marketers is the 2025 access expansion, not the product launch. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
An influencer with recognized authority in a category, such as beauty, tech, or lifestyle, distinguished from a KOC, an everyday user whose reviews read as authentic.

KOL terminology originated in medical and scientific fields and is long established in Chinese social commerce platforms such as Xiaohongshu and Douyin. It is now crossing into Western marketing vocabulary as TikTok Shop and cross-border commerce push agencies and brands outside China to adopt the same tiered creator strategy, using KOLs for reach and KOCs for social proof. This is directly relevant to Turkiye and MEA marketers running cross-border TikTok Shop campaigns.
Reacherapp and multiple TikTok Shop growth guides explicitly frame "KOL" as the term Western brands scaling on TikTok Shop need to learn, importing it from the China playbook.
KOL, bir kategoride tanınmış otoriteye sahip bir influencer'dır ve incelemeleri daha samimi görünen sıradan bir kullanıcı olan KOC'tan ayrılır.

Meta's ad product, publicly rebranded Collaborative Ads, that lets a brand and a retail or marketplace partner co-run Facebook and Instagram ads using the retailer's catalog and audience data.

CPAS directs ad clicks to the retailer's own product pages rather than the brand's site. The product launched around 2019-2020 but expanded materially into quick-commerce and additional regional marketplace partnerships in 2025. It acts as a direct bridge between social advertising and commerce or retail media, and its retailer network keeps growing into markets relevant to Turkiye and MEA; Trendyol lists CPAS as one of its four core ad models.

Meta, "How Meta's Collaborative Ads Are Fueling Quick Commerce Boom In India" (about.fb.com, December 2025); Trendyol seller guides list CPAS (Facebook/Instagram) alongside product and store ads as a core advertising model.
CPAS, bir markanın perakende veya pazaryeri ortağıyla, ortağın katalogunu ve kitle verisini kullanarak Facebook ve Instagram reklamlarını birlikte yürütmesini sağlayan Meta reklam ürünüdür.
Product predates the window; included because its retailer footprint and marketer relevance (including Trendyol in the Turkiye market) expanded materially within 2024-2026. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.
A managed, modular technology and services model that lets a retailer launch a full retail media business, including ad serving, campaign management, and reporting, without building it in-house.

RMaaS is a label that vendors began using in 2024-2025; as of 2026 it is documented mainly by vendor announcements rather than independent trade coverage. The model targets mid-size and regional retailers, including those in Türkiye and MEA, that want to launch a retail media network without building the technology themselves. Marketers evaluating new retail media partners may see it used to describe fully managed setups.
Adhese, "Adhese launches Retail Media as a Service (RMaaS), strengthening leadership team with two key hires" (2025).

Weakest-sourced item in this set: primarily documented via one vendor's own announcement (Adhese) plus a competing RMAAS.net product name; not yet confirmed as an industry-standard term via independent trade press (Digiday/eMarketer searches did not surface independent RMaaS coverage). The practice of making AI-assisted work look fully human-made, through handcrafted styling, named creators or behind-the-scenes stories, while hiding how much AI actually did.

Humanwashing is the mirror image of AI washing: instead of overstating AI to borrow a tech halo, a brand understates AI to protect an authenticity halo. Business ethicist Peter Seele introduced 'humanwashing of machines' in a March 2021 post, and in 2022 formalized it with Andreea Scorici and Mario Schultz in AI & Society as the deceptive use of a machine's human-like appearance to mislead people about what it can really do. Marketing writers then took the word over for brand and creative work: the WHAT'S ANU newsletter in December 2025, followed by agencies such as Flux+Form in 2026, where it now means passing off AI-generated content as human craft. The risk for marketers is trust: when undisclosed AI use surfaces, the brand is judged less on the AI itself than on the concealment.

In August 2025 J.Crew posted AI-generated images styled as vintage catalog shots on Instagram without saying they were AI-made. After the newsletter Blackbird Spyplane exposed them on 26 August 2025, the brand edited its captions to credit an 'AI photographer' rather than stating plainly that the images were AI-generated.
AI Washing, Synthetic Trust, Synthetic Influence, Responsible AI, Greenwashing
Humanwashing, yapay zeka ile üretilen bir işi el emeği görünümü, isimlendirilmiş yaratıcılar ya da kamera arkası hikâyelerle tamamen insan yapımı gibi sunarak yapay zekanın katkısını gizlemektir.

Recency: no source dated in the last 14 days uses the exact word; the topic is current through adjacent coverage (Schaefer, 21 Sep 2026). Seele's original sense differs from the marketing sense; both are stated. Fact-checked 2026-09-23.

The question sits in the territory of MMA's AI Leadership Think Tank (ALTT, formerly the AI Leadership Coalition), which runs a Responsible AI working group and the Responsible AI Innovation Lab (RAIL), a source of guidelines, templates and checklists for ethical AI use in marketing. It is also the counterpart of AI Washing, already in this dictionary: one overclaims AI, the other hides it, and both erode the same asset, consumer trust.

A marketing or advertising technology stack assembled from many separately bought tools that were bolted together over time and do not work as one system.

A Frankenstack is what a marketing team ends up with when each department buys its own tools for data, media buying, creative and reporting, and the pieces are later wired together with manual work, exports and custom connectors. The word blends Frankenstein and tech stack: a system built from mismatched parts that runs, but badly. It comes from the martech world. The earliest verifiable use found is a 31 March 2015 chiefmartec.com post by its editor Scott Brinker, who wrote that the phrase had entered the industry's lingo; six weeks later, in a CIO.com interview, he called it a 'humorous label' for stacks that grew out of marketing silos. No single coiner is known. In 2025 and 2026 the term returned in adtech coverage as teams started adding AI tools and agents on top of these stacks. Before a team adds another AI tool, it pays to check whether the tool connects the existing data and workflows or just adds one more part to the stack.

In the 8 September 2026 episode of MMA's Decoding AI for Marketing podcast, hosted by Greg Stuart and Rex Briggs, Fluency CEO Mike Lane described advertising execution as still largely manual. The episode notes say that when fragmented platforms are stitched together with new AI tools, they can create what Lane calls a 'Frankenstack' of software, and that he argues for integrated operating systems that connect data, media and AI agents. At Advertising Week 2025, adtech company Infillion framed the trend as 'the end of the Frankenstack' and a move to composable ad tech (Infillion blog, 9 October 2025).

Frankenstack, zamanla ayrı ayrı alınıp birbirine eklenen ve tek bir sistem gibi çalışmayan araçlardan oluşan pazarlama ya da reklam teknolojisi altyapısıdır.

No public transcript of the episode; Mike Lane's wording is attributed through the episode notes, not quoted directly. March 2015 is the earliest verifiable use, not a proven coinage date. MMA names checked against mma-org-context. Fact-checked 2026-09-28.
